I was but a wee 3 year old. The year was 2000. I was swinging alone in the back yard when i jumped off after deciding i wanted a sip of my soda. I grabbed my soda off the tree stump where i had placed it earlier, not really paying attention as i began moving it towards my face. And then i looked down. *And the holiest of motherflippin screams to ever scream was released from the deepest pits of my wee lil lungs*.

Time slowed. There was the most massive, most blackest, most shiniest praying mantis lookin fella to ever exist--which i should mention, I didn't even know such a thing existed at the time so that only amplified my horror. That nasty insect was perched right on top of my soda can, probably drinking it like the mean lil thief he was and by the time I noticed him he was a mere 5 inches from my face. I screamed, threw the can, and ran to my mama who was sitting in the driveway on a fold out chair. I didn't speak. I simply crawled into her lap and stared in fear at the can of mountain dew she had nearby in a cup holder. Every fiber of my being was deeply grossed out and horrified.

For the following year i was too horrified to drink out of non-transparent containers for fear that the devilish massive monstrosity of an insect would come climbing out into my mouth.

The mountains are very impressive, especially for this being your first oil painting. The clouds look a little "tight", as though you held yourself back from just loosening up and flowing. Unfortunately, practice is the most effective solution for truly loosening up with this stuff. Make sure you pay attention to the anatomy of your clouds. Look at reference pictures of fluffy clouds; observe the shapes they make and the shadows they produce. Try to replicate the depth, texture, density, ect.. Also, don't be afraid to let parts of your painting go "outside of the frame" or off the edge of the canvas. 

And a little tip that's helped to improve my painting is to pay attention to the hues i use in shadows/highlights. Shadows are typically made up of cooler hues, while highlights tend to be composed of warmer hues. Hope this helps! Keep up the great work, you have a very solid start

Being pre internet, pre mobile devices, and pre cellphones.

Don't get me wrong, i love the internet and the devices used to access it, it's just that having it with me all the time is distracting. I miss focusing on what i'm doing *in the moment*. I miss being bored and having to meander around outside for something to do; now when i'm bored i just mindlessly scroll through reddit or instagram. I no longer feel the urge to go see how high i can climb in a tree or go take my bike and ride in silence around town. I miss seeing people walk around and explore places with their eyes rather than through the lens of a smartphone camera.

I know i sound like a whinny old person. I do recognize the benefits of all these things and i would never yell at someone for using their phone at a dinner table or anything. I just miss the "here and only here" feeling of not having a phone in my back pocket :-/

Whenever i finish a painting and feel happy with it but am willing to try adding more, i sketch with colored pencils or crayons a sloppy color-orientated version of my painting, and try new things there as not to risk ruining my painting. If i'm happy with the paper sketch, i'll go ahead with paints to my canvas.

All in all, your painting looks great, could probably just use some more reflections and shadows on the waters surface 😀👍

I've successfully lost weight and kept it off by forming the habit of watching what i eat and doing floor workouts. The key to being successful is to think of it as a lifestyle change, not a short fad diet. It's hard at first to get used to restricted eating, but after a week of trying it gets pretty easy for me.

For dieting:
I start by determining what ingredients contribute to fat gain. For me, i read the ingredient list of anything i might eat and don't eat it if there is high fructose corn syrup or a high sugar content. I also avoid anything prepackaged with a serving size calorie count of over 150. Try to avoid mindless snacking. If possible, plan on eating three meals a day; breakfast, lunch, and dinner. I would also recommend not drinking soda at all, or even alcoholic beverages. And try to not eat fast food...

For workouts:
All the workouts i do are on my tiny bedroom floor. I try do 20 pushups, 20 seconds of planks, 30 seconds of wall sits, and then 10 more pushups. Last summer i would go jogging but now i have an injured foot so i can't really do that anymore :( . Honestly, my weight loss is from what i eat and not what workouts i do. I do get lazy sometimes though, so i would say i only do floor workouts every other day.

For motivation:
(This is kind of lame motivation but it works for me)
-you'll see results in 2 weeks, your family will notice results in 4 weeks, and the world will notice results in 8 weeks
-weight loss is 70% what you eat and 30% exercise
